newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota hopes to market driverless bus.
newsitem.headline: Toyota hopes to market driverless bus.

text.p: Japanese car giant Toyota Motor Corp said on Friday it hopes to market driverless buses for public use.
"We are thinking of commercialising the automated vehicle control system," a Toyota spokeswoman said, but she did not say when the driverless buses would actually debut.
The automated system consists of an array of sensors placed on highways and a vehicle also equipped with sensors to ensure it stays in its lane.
The system is cost-efficient compared with conventional rail or monorail systems, with some estimates putting construction at one-third the cost of laying down tracks for commuter trains.
Toyota also said that buses would use Toyota's newly developed "hybrid engine," which is powered by a small engine and an electric motor.

Cars using the new engine are expected to cut down on both fuel consumption and emissions of carbon dioxide by 50 percent compared with a standard gasoline engine. Other emissions would be cut to one-tenth of current levels.
The hybrid engine is started by its electric motor and the gasoline engine kicks in when the vehicle accelerates and runs at cruising speeds.
One Japanese newspaper said Toyota may install the vehicle system at the World Expo to be held in Aichi Prefecture, central Japan, in 2005, but Toyota officials would not confirm the report.
